title: Derived quasi-coherent modules on an affine scheme
statement: Let $A$ be a ring and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-pc-scheme]. The functor $M^\bullet\mapsto\widetilde{M^\bullet}$ (termwise associated quasi-coherent sheaf) induces an equivalence of triangulated categories $D(A)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-pc-derived-category], with quasi-inverse the derived global sections functor $R\Gamma(Y,-)$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image]; it sends $A[k]$ to $\mathcal O_Y[k]$ for every $k\in\mathbf Z$.

proof.text: Exactness of $M\mapsto\widetilde M$ as a functor $\mathrm{Mod}_A\to\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$, and $\widetilde A\cong\mathcal O_Y$. By clause (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] the functor preserves cokernels, so it is right exact. Let $u:M\to N$ be injective and $\mathcal K=\ker\widetilde u$; $\mathcal K$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel] ($\widetilde M,\widetilde N$ are quasi-coherent by definition, taking $U=Y$). Since kernels in $\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$ are sectionwise, $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal K)=\ker(\Gamma(Y,\widetilde u))$, which under the unit isomorphisms of clause (2) is $\ker u=0$; by clause (3), $\mathcal K\cong\widetilde{\Gamma(Y,\mathcal K)}=0$. A right exact functor preserving monomorphisms preserves short exact sequences, hence is exact. Finally clause (1) gives $\operatorname{Hom}(\widetilde A,\mathcal F)\cong\Gamma(Y,\mathcal F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_Y,\mathcal F)$ naturally in $\mathcal F$, so $\widetilde A\cong\mathcal O_Y$ by Yoneda. (The abelian adjunction is not an equivalence onto $\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$, only onto quasi-coherent modules, so left exactness needs the kernel statement: Stacks, Schemes, Lemma 26.7.5, schemes-lemma-spec-sheaves, as used in the proof of Tag 06Z0.)

proof.text: The functors and the comparison maps. By Step 1, termwise $\widetilde{\ }$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms and cones, so it induces a triangulated functor $D(A)\to D(\mathcal O_Y)$ with $H^i(\widetilde{M^\bullet})\cong\widetilde{H^i(M^\bullet)}$, which is quasi-coherent; so it lands in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. $R\Gamma(Y,-)$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image] is computed by $R\Gamma(Y,E)=\Gamma(Y,I^\bullet)$ for a K-injective complex $I^\bullet$ quasi-isomorphic to $E$, and is triangulated. Define $a_E:\widetilde{\Gamma(Y,I^\bullet)}\to I^\bullet\cong E$ as the termwise counit of clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], and $b_M:M^\bullet\to\Gamma(Y,\widetilde{M^\bullet})\to\Gamma(Y,I^\bullet)=R\Gamma(Y,\widetilde{M^\bullet})$ as the termwise unit followed by $\Gamma$ of a K-injective resolution $\widetilde{M^\bullet}\to I^\bullet$. Both are natural in the derived categories (homotopy-uniqueness of K-injective resolutions). It remains to show that $a_E$ ($E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$) and $b_M$ are quasi-isomorphisms; then the two triangulated functors are quasi-inverse.

source.place: Tag 06Z0, proof (elucidation: adjunction mappings a and b)

proof.text: For $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ and every $i$, $H^i(R\Gamma(Y,E))\cong\Gamma(Y,H^i(E))$ naturally. By shifting, take $i=0$. The functor $F=\Gamma(Y,-)$ commutes with products, and $R^pF(\mathcal F)=H^p(Y,\mathcal F)=0$ for quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$ and $p\ge1$ by [lem-pc-affine-vanishing]; so [lem-pc-unbounded-derived-functor-cohomological-bound] applies with $N=1$. Take the truncation triangle $\tau_{\le-1}E\to E\to\tau_{\ge0}E\to$; both truncations lie in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ (their cohomology sheaves are among those of $E$). With $b=-1$ the cited bound gives $H^j(R\Gamma(Y,\tau_{\le-1}E))=0$ for $j\ge0$, so the long exact sequence gives $H^0(R\Gamma(Y,E))\cong H^0(R\Gamma(Y,\tau_{\ge0}E))$. The bounded-below $\tau_{\ge0}E$ has an injective resolution $I^\bullet$ in degrees $\ge0$, and left exactness of $\Gamma$ gives $H^0(\Gamma(Y,I^\bullet))=\Gamma(Y,\ker(I^0\to I^1))=\Gamma(Y,H^0(E))$. (This replaces the earlier detour through $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, where identifying $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z,H^i(Rf_*E))$ with $H^i(R\Gamma(Y,E))$ for unbounded $E$ is the same unproved statement.)

The counit $a_E$ is a quasi-isomorphism for $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$: by exactness (Step 1) and Step 3, $H^i(\widetilde{R\Gamma(Y,E)})\cong\widetilde{H^i(R\Gamma(Y,E))}\cong\widetilde{\Gamma(Y,H^i(E))}$, and $H^i(a_E)$ is the counit $\widetilde{\Gamma(Y,H^i(E))}\to H^i(E)$, an isomorphism by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] since $H^i(E)$ is quasi-coherent. In particular every object of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ is isomorphic to $\widetilde{R\Gamma(Y,E)}$ (essential surjectivity). The unit $b_M$ is a quasi-isomorphism: by Step 3 applied to $\widetilde{M^\bullet}\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ and Step 2, $H^i(R\Gamma(Y,\widetilde{M^\bullet}))\cong\Gamma(Y,\widetilde{H^i(M^\bullet)})$, and $H^i(b_M)$ is the unit $H^i(M^\bullet)\to\Gamma(Y,\widetilde{H^i(M^\bullet)})$, an isomorphism by clause (2). Hence the functors are quasi-inverse equivalences of triangulated categories.
